text.p: Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd said on Thursday that calendar 1996 net profits from its Australian and Indonesian coal operations fell by 12 percent to US$178 million.
The group said in a statement accompanying its overall profit result that coal production fell one percent to 26.1 million tonnes.
"There was increased competition in the international market for steaming coal in 1996," RTZ-CRA said.

"The demand outlook for steaming coal, however, is robust with projections over the next 10 years being well in excess of economic growth. Coking coal growth is expected to be more modest even though the market was strong in 1996," it said.
The company said its Australian operations were adversely affected by labour problems and operational setbacks.
In Indonesia, the half-owned Kaltim Prima steaming coal mine increased production by 12 percent to lift the group's share to 4.9 million tonnes.
Kaltim's net profit contribution increased to US$51 million from US$43 million while sales rose by US$30 million to US$205 million.
The mining house said production by its U.S. coal operation Kennecott Energy rose by three percent to 40.9 million tonnes.
Kennecott Energy's net profit fell to US$61 million from $72 million in 1995 and turnover fell by $20 million to $357 million.
